text: Brindle Viaduct strengthening work revised from eighteen months and £2.4 million to nine months and £3.1 million, with modifications including more night work, steel deck, and weekend closures beginning October.
The upper path at Ganister Tarn remains open despite online rumors. The car park-boathouse link closed September 1st for bank stabilisation, reopening before Christmas.
Quernmore's bottle kiln requires repairs after survey. It leans dangerously at the crown. Recommendations include grouting and rebuilding the top. The trust has secured partial funding.
Hessle Low Mill received a £74,000 grant for cap and sails work, while Hessle High Mill's application was refused because it was deemed too deteriorated.
Bus 831 between Cotterdale and Hawes runs Saturdays only from November after Tuesday withdrawal due to low ridership. A minibus trial starts Tuesdays in January.
A 2026 breeding-bird survey at Alder Carr recorded 46 pairs of willow tit, the highest since 2011, attributed to expanded wet woodland habitat and mild spring conditions.

The Priory gatehouse undergoes twelve-week February renovation for stone replacement, repointing, and roof renewal, staying open except during April roof work; precinct wall assessment is scheduled for autumn.

Permission for the Larkfield quarry extension was granted Tuesday, subject to conditions: bat survey completion, road widening at Pitt Lane, and restricting lorry movements to 48 daily, none before 07:00. Survey expected spring.

Ryhope pool reopened 19 August after new plant room flooded during commissioning, delaying opening from 3 June. Italian circulation pump replacement was required. Opens at 06:30 weekdays, thirty minutes earlier, with diving boards pending inspection.

At Bewick, licence refusal rates fell from 9 to 6 percent despite refusals rising from 41 to 58, as applications nearly doubled. Of 14 appeals, 9 succeeded, with growth attributed to the new late-night levy exemption.

Coldbeck Co-operative Society purchased the auction mart at Stang Bridge, not the Coldbeck Foot mill site. The mart will house a food store and eleven flats. The mill remains on the market with another buyer in early negotiations.
